item.title: The Information reports at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia hardware reached Chinese companies since 2023 through a network linked to a Megaspeed executive
item.description: The Information reported on 10 November 2026, citing two people familiar, that at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia hardware has been shipped to Chinese companies since 2023 through a network linked to Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom US officials reportedly concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset (New York Times, 29 October). Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation, President Trump said the FBI is looking into it, and a shareholder class action was filed in San Jose; Nvidia shares fell a further 4% to 6% on 10 November after a roughly 4% drop on 9 November. Caveat: single-source figure, not confirmed by Nvidia or US authorities, and the export-control status of the shipments is not established. Country conversion: if borne out, a multi-billion-dollar leak of US accelerators into China via Singapore, inviting tighter end-use checks. [Signal 48, Single-source, via The Information via Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov 2026; CNBC, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Norway halts new grid reservations for data centres until as late as 1 August 2027 and plans a licensing regime
item.description: Norway's transmission operator Statnett on 9 November 2026 paused new grid capacity reservations for data centres and the processing of new facility-functionality approvals, including applications already received for plants on the 420 kV grid, until new technical requirements are approved by the regulator RME, expected no later than 1 August 2027. The same day the government said it will introduce a licensing (concession) regime for existing and future data centres, favouring those serving defence, emergency services, health and other critical functions, and said crypto mining will not count as socially useful. Statnett figures: about 800 MW connected, 4.2 GW reserved, 9.1 GW in the queue and a further 18 GW requested, against national peak demand of just over 25 GW. Caveat: connected and already-approved facilities are unaffected, and Statnett may still process some smaller plants due before August 2027. Country conversion: one of Europe's cheapest-power hosts closes its queue to new large AI loads for up to nine months. [Signal 58, Confirmed, via Norwegian Government and Statnett releases, 9 Nov 2026; DCD; DLA Piper; Enerdata] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SpaceX files for a roughly $24 billion gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility at Starbase, Texas
item.description: Reuters reported on 9 November 2026, citing a public hearing notice, that SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas with an estimated $24 billion of capital investment for its initial phases, and has applied for a property tax abatement and an economic development agreement that the Starbase City Commission will consider on 9 December. SpaceX would build, own and operate the facilities; an affiliate has filed for an 8-mile gas pipeline to Starbase due in service by January 2027. Caveat: the notice gives no generating capacity or compute scale, and the abatement size and term are undisclosed; this sits alongside the separate Cochise County, Arizona filing heard the same day. Country conversion: a second behind-the-meter frontier campus filing in Texas despite the extended state pause. [Signal 44, Single-source, via Reuters, 9 Nov 2026 (Starbase public hearing notice)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SoftBank, Grab and PETROS sign joint development agreements with $1.85 billion seed capital for Malaysian AI infrastructure targeting 5 GW
item.description: SoftBank Group and Grab announced on 9 November 2026 joint development agreements, with Sarawak's state oil company PETROS, for $1.85 billion of initial combined seed capital to build AI infrastructure in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of 5 GW or more. The Sarawak project is $1 billion ($800 million SoftBank, $100 million Grab, $100 million PETROS), building on an 8 October Kuching framework agreement; the Peninsular project is $850 million ($650 million Grab, $200 million SoftBank), led by Grab. SoftBank agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up on Grab shares it holds directly. Caveat: capital is staged against development and customer-contract milestones; JV formation and investment terms remain subject to definitive agreements, and no hyperscaler customer, site size or power contract is named yet. Country conversion: a second gigawatt-scale Malaysian programme in a week after Google's $15 billion commitment. [Signal 52, Confirmed, via SoftBank Group and Grab joint release, 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Israel's National AI Directorate sets a 300,000-GPU, 2 GW sovereign AI target and a domestic frontier model
item.description: Erez Askal, head of the National AI Directorate in Israel's Prime Minister's Office, presented the national AI strategy at Tel Aviv University's AI & Cyber Week on 9 November 2026 (Ctech): a sovereign AI stack with about 300,000 GPUs (100,000 for academia, government, defence and startups; 200,000 for technology companies and data centres), about 2 GW of electricity capacity for AI infrastructure, data centres and semiconductor manufacturing, and an Israeli frontier model built with partner countries. Caveat: these are targets from a conference presentation; no budget, timeline, sites or vendors were given, and Ctech notes Israel's grid is already strained by data centre demand. Country conversion: Israel states a quantified sovereign compute goal for the first time. [Signal 34, Single-source, via Ctech (Calcalist), 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Anthropic buys about $3.4 billion of commitments for 1.7 GW of gas-fired generators from OnePWR, FT reports
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 8 November 2026, and CNBC carried, that Anthropic bought commitments for 1.7 GW of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from San Antonio-based OnePWR Solutions in late September for about $3.4 billion, including the engineering and construction capability to install them. Anthropic did not acquire OnePWR and no staff moved; secondary coverage says the deal took over OnePWR's existing Caterpillar orders. Caveat: FT is the only primary source and cites one person familiar; Anthropic has not confirmed, and sites for the generators are not disclosed. Country conversion: a frontier lab is buying its own US behind-the-meter generation queue position, roughly $2 million per MW, alongside its Riot and TeraWulf leases. [Signal 46, Single-source, via Financial Times via CNBC, 8 Nov 2026; DCD, 9 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: PPL's Invitium agrees terms to build about 2 GW of generation for QTS in Salem Township, Pennsylvania; advanced-stage pipeline reaches 35.3 GW
item.description: On its Q3 2026 call (6 November) PPL said Invitium Energy, its 51% joint venture with Blackstone Infrastructure, agreed all key commercial terms under a letter of intent with QTS for about 2 GW of generation for QTS's Salem Township, Luzerne County data centre: two combined-cycle gas plants plus fuel cells and battery storage, a 20-year initial term with five-year renewals, and an estimated $5 billion to $7 billion of project investment at $2,500 to $3,500 per kW. Fuel cells and batteries could be online from 2029 and the gas plants in 2032 and 2033. PPL's advanced-stage Pennsylvania data centre pipeline rose for an 11th straight quarter to 35.3 GW (up 3.5 GW), with about 11.4 GW under signed service agreements and 8.5 GW under construction (up 2 GW); 300 MW is energised so far. Caveat: the QTS terms are non-binding pending a long-form agreement, and PPL's plan excludes Invitium. Country conversion: a US utility building dedicated generation for a single campus rather than waiting on PJM. [Signal 50, Confirmed, via PPL Q3 2026 earnings call, 6 Nov 2026; DCD, 10 Nov 2026; Lehigh Valley Business] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Equinix opens SG6, among the first Singapore data centres built under the post-moratorium call-for-application regime
item.description: Equinix opened SG6, its sixth Singapore IBX, on 6 November 2026 with an initial investment of about $290 million, 8 MW and about 1,550 cabinets in phase one and up to 20 MW at full build-out. Equinix says SG6 is among the first data centres developed under Singapore's Data Centre Call for Application framework, designed for liquid-cooled GPU deployments at a target PUE of 1.20; a co-innovation facility with NUS follows in 2027. Singapore's Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How gave the launch keynote. Caveat: capacity is small next to Johor and Batam campuses across the border. Country conversion: Singapore's controlled-allocation regime is now delivering live AI-ready capacity. [Signal 30, Confirmed, via Equinix release, 6 Nov 2026; MDDI keynote; DCD, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: SpaceXAI applies for a 747-acre, up to 6 GW data centre campus in Cochise County, Arizona; zoning decision 9 December
item.description: SpaceXAI, via affiliate Tombstone Resources LLC, has applied to Cochise County, Arizona for a special development permit for up to nine 493,000 sq ft data centre buildings on 747 acres near the Willcox Playa, on land owned by AEPCO and Southline Transmission and adjacent to AEPCO's 626 MW Apache Generating Station (DCD, 6 November 2026). The application describes four 1.5 GW phases, construction from March 2027 if zoning is approved, about $3.6 billion of company-funded power infrastructure ($500 million for Phase I) and a 24 GWh battery system. The county decision is set for 9 December. Caveat: 6 GW is the company's full-build claim; timing depends on grid upgrades, and chips, power and cooling to fill it are not secured. Country conversion: a gigawatt-class US campus filed outside the Texas pause map. [Signal 44, Corroborated, via DCD, 6 Nov 2026 (Cochise County application); Arizona Daily Star; Data Center Feed] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kazakhstan signs preliminary deals with Gaw Capital, Boosteroid and Firebird for 480 MW more at Ekibastuz Data Center Valley
item.description: Kazakhstan's prime minister's office said on 6 November 2026 that Gaw Capital, Boosteroid and Firebird signed preliminary agreements adding a combined 480 MW at Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz (second phase), with talks on a further 240 MW with China Energy, Aleria and Energy Capital Global; no per-company split was given (Southward Tech, 9 November). The government targets 1 GW by 2029. Phase one is three centres totalling 304 MW: a 68 MW site targeted for Q2 2027, Firebird's 164 MW site with excavation 70% complete, and a 72 MW centre in Q4. Firebird said in October it holds a US export licence for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs. Caveat: the new deals are preliminary and come via a government statement. Country conversion: Kazakhstan adds phase-two demand from both US and Chinese-linked parties. [Signal 32, Single-source, via Southward Tech, 9 Nov 2026 (Kazakhstan PM office, 6 Nov)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: TeraWulf locks Fluor EPC and a Google credit backstop for Anthropic's ~401 MW Justified campus in Kentucky
item.description: TeraWulf's 6 November 2026 Q3 release and Fluor's 4 November newsroom say the companies signed a definitive EPC for three data centre buildings at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, with early works already underway and Fluor to recognize the award in Q4 once pricing for the first two buildings is finalized. TeraWulf states a 20-year Anthropic lease for about 401 MW of critical IT capacity (~$19 billion contracted revenue over the initial term), a Google credit backstop for anticipated project financing supporting that lease, and phased ready-for-service from late 2027 through Q2 2028. Separately TeraWulf lifted Muskie contracted power from 500 MW to 1,000 MW subject to Kentucky PSC approval. Caveat: site development capex ex-compute is cited in investor materials around $4.0–4.5 billion in secondary summaries; stick to the IR/Fluor figures above for Wire. Country conversion: Anthropic offtake plus investment-grade-linked financing and named EPC move a Kentucky GW-class campus into construction. [Signal 57, Confirmed, via TeraWulf IR, 6 Nov 2026; Fluor newsroom, 4 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: EuroHPC voids all AI gigafactory tenders for technical reasons; large sites due 3 December, medium sites pushed to 4 February
item.description: The EuroHPC Joint Undertaking updated its AI Gigafactory call (EUROHPC-2026-CEI-AIGF-01) on 5 November 2026: for undisclosed technical reasons all draft and submitted tenders in the system will not be considered and must be recreated under new submission links. The deadline for Lot 1 is extended to 4 February 2027 to give member states time to complete required steps, while Lot 2 stays at 3 December 2026, both 17:00 Luxembourg time. DCD (10 November) describes the programme as four smaller sites eligible for up to EUR 100 million each in Phase I and three larger sites up to EUR 200 million each. Caveat: DCD's report reverses which lot moved; this item follows the EuroHPC call page. Country conversion: Europe's sovereign compute procurement slips again, and no site awards are possible before 2027. [Signal 46, Confirmed, via EuroHPC JU call page (updated 5 Nov 2026); DCD, 10 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: About 600,000 Nvidia H200s sit in Hong Kong as Beijing withholds large-scale import approval, Reuters reports
item.description: Reuters reported exclusively on 5 November 2026, citing two people familiar, that about 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China because Beijing has not approved large-volume imports. Several major Chinese internet companies have each received about 10,000 H200s in recent months and small quantities have moved via intermediaries. One person said an eight-card H200 server was offered for more than 6 million yuan (about $900,000) in mainland China by end-October, about three times a year earlier, and Blackwell servers for more than 20 million yuan. Caveat: Reuters is the only source; MIIT, NDRC, Nvidia and the Chinese buyers did not comment. Country conversion stall: US-licensed supply exists but China's own approvals are the binding constraint. [Signal 42, Single-source, via Reuters via Investing.com, 5 Nov 2026; DCD, 6 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Texas governor-elect commits to keep the data centre moratorium until new laws pass; analysts put about half the US hyperscale pipeline at risk
item.description: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said she will extend outgoing governor Greg Abbott's pause on new data centres, which she called a scam, until the legislature enacts her Texans First Data Center Priorities: local votes on projects, no NDAs, proof households will not pay more for power or water, no subsidies, union labour, and water contracts voidable if they threaten community supply (DCD, 5 Nov). BMI estimates 53% of hyperscaler pipeline growth sits in newly flipped governor states (Texas, Georgia, Ohio, plus Pennsylvania, where Josh Shapiro was re-elected) and says the Texas pause could plausibly run into late 2027; Cleanview counts 159 GW, or 41% of planned US data centres, in states whose new governors back a pause. Caveat: Hinojosa takes office in January 2027, ERCOT expects its large-load review to end in December, and BMI calls a national moratorium low-probability; the pipeline figures are analyst estimates, not cancellations. Country conversion: Texas, the largest US growth market, is now set to stay paused past the audit. [Signal 64, Corroborated, via DCD, 5 Nov 2026 (Hinojosa; BMI and Cleanview report); Hinojosa campaign release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: US voters back data centre restrictions in 40 of 41 local ballot measures; OpenAI answers with a Compute Campus Policy
item.description: Of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states on 3 November, voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures in all but one, per Ballotpedia and CNBC (Axios counts 43-1 with about 75% average support). On 5 November OpenAI published a Compute Campus Policy and National Community Compact: for data centres it owns and operates it will seek community input, publish construction plans, stop using NDAs with public officials and pay the full cost of its power, and it urged lawmakers to write similar rules into law. Reuters reported the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 8% on 5 November and CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 11% and 15%; UBS estimated about 30% of expected 2028 US capacity additions could be at risk. Caveat: OpenAI's commitments cover only sites it owns and operates, not leased capacity; ballot counts differ slightly by tally. Country conversion: US siting now carries explicit community and ratepayer conditions. [Signal 58, Corroborated, via CNBC, 5 Nov 2026; Axios, 5 Nov 2026; DCD; Reuters via Investing.com] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Microsoft declines an option to more than double its Texas compute contract with Nscale
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 5 November 2026, and Reuters confirmed via a person familiar, that Microsoft will not exercise an option to more than double its existing agreement with Nscale in Texas, a potential extension worth tens of billions of dollars. Per DCD, Microsoft already operates about 230 MW at Nscale's leased Ionic Digital site in Barstow; the declined option, which Nscale says was closer to 500 MW, was for behind-the-meter capacity at Nscale's own adjacent Ward County site. The source says the decision was made months ago, before Nscale's September IPO filing, and does not change its disclosed $103 billion backlog, about 40% of it Microsoft; Nscale has since signed Figure for 100,000 Vera Rubin GPUs at the site and is talking to other customers including hyperscalers. Caveat: FT is the primary source; Microsoft and Nscale did not comment. Country conversion: a hyperscaler passes on gigawatt-scale Texas neocloud capacity weeks after exiting Nscale's Essex site. [Signal 48, Corroborated, via FT via Reuters (Investing.com), 5 Nov 2026; DCD, 5 Nov 2026; AFR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Princeton Digital Group secures about $1.3 billion of green financing for its 200 MW JH1 campus in Johor
item.description: Princeton Digital Group announced this week about $1.3 billion (about RM5.1 billion) of green financing, underwritten by Affin Bank, HSBC, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, to continue building its JH1 campus at Sedenak Tech Park, Johor. JH1 is designed for 200 MW of high-density AI and cloud load; its first 52 MW phase was completed in July 2025 and a third building topped out in late 2025. Caveat: no tenant or new MW timing was disclosed. Country conversion: Johor capacity keeps converting into bank-financed build, a day after Google added $15 billion for Malaysia. [Signal 40, Confirmed, via DCD, 5 Nov 2026 (PDG announcement)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: IndiaAI's next 10,000-GPU compute round halves the entry bar to 512 units; bids close 13 November
item.description: C-DAC's request for empanelment (RFE C-DAC/GPU/01/2026, issued 7 October) for the IndiaAI Mission seeks up to 10,000 GPUs, TPUs and other accelerators, with bidders needing 512 units at a single Indian data centre, half the 1,000-unit bar of the first round. After two corrigenda, bids close 13 November and technical bids open 14 November. Providers serve five years with data, control planes and backups kept in India, must have at least INR 120 crore average turnover, and can qualify with a purchase order backed by a INR 10 crore guarantee. The existing IndiaAI portal lists 45,081 units, led by 16,496 H100, with lowest bids of INR 153 per H100-hour on demand. Caveat: single trade-press report of a government document; Stage 1 sets no prices, and new capacity may not go live until late 2027. Country conversion: India widens its sovereign compute pool to smaller domestic operators. [Signal 36, Single-source, via Communications Today, 5 Nov 2026 (C-DAC RFE)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Google commits $17 billion to its first Wyoming data centre, paired with a 702 MW fuel-cell CCS plant
item.description: Google announced on 5 November 2026 its first data centre in Wyoming, a long-term $17 billion investment in Laramie County with partners Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy, American Electric Power and Related Digital. The campus is contracted with AEP for a commercial-scale 702 MW natural-gas fuel-cell development with carbon capture and storage — Bloom Energy cells, geologic storage at Tallgrass's Eastern Wyoming Sequestration Hub — and will be air-cooled to cut local water use; Google says it will pay for 100% of the power it uses and cover growth-driven infrastructure. Reuters and WyoFile corroborate the same day; the 702 MW Bloom package builds on earlier AEP/Black Hills Cheyenne power filings already on Wire. Caveat: Google did not publish a campus IT-MW or first-power date. Country conversion: a hyperscaler locks a multi-billion Wyoming offtake after midterm data-centre backlash. [Signal 58, Confirmed, via Google blog, 5 Nov 2026; Reuters, 5 Nov 2026; WyoFile, 5 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Amazon confirms a Somervell County data centre campus as direct offtaker from Comanche Peak nuclear
item.description: Amazon's US Press Center said on 5 November 2026 it is advancing a data centre campus in unincorporated Somervell County near Glen Rose on Vistra land beside the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant, with site preparation underway and at least 550 full-time jobs. Power is to flow on dedicated transmission to an on-site substation with Amazon as a direct nuclear offtaker paying the full energy cost; cooling water comes from the Comanche Creek industrial reservoir under existing Vistra surface rights (projected use under 2% of those rights), not local drinking supplies. Secondary reporting (CryptoBriefing; Texas PUC agenda coverage) frames the project as roughly $5 billion, up to 18 buildings on about 435 acres, and a 20-year PPA for up to 1,200 MW with initial energization targeted late 2027 — those dollar and MW figures are not in Amazon's 5 Nov community post. Caveat: local approvals and PPA buyer identity were reported earlier in 2026; today's post is the clearest public campus confirmation amid Texas's large-load pause. Country conversion: hyperscaler nuclear conversion advances in Texas while ERCOT's audit runs to December. [Signal 52, Corroborated, via Amazon US Press Center, 5 Nov 2026; CryptoBriefing, 5 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Riot leases its whole 910 MW Corsicana, Texas campus to Anthropic for about $28 billion over 15 years
item.description: Riot Platforms' Q3 release (4 November 2026) announced a 15-year triple-net powered land lease with a 'leading Frontier AI Lab' for its entire Corsicana campus in Navarro County, Texas: 910 MW of critical IT capacity on 332 acres, about $28 billion of contract value and about $1.8 billion average annual rent, rising to about $54 billion if both five-year extensions are exercised. Riot's 10-Q names the tenant as Anthropic PBC (signed 28 October, effective 4 November) with base rent of $130 per kW-month escalating 3% a year. Delivery: 400 MW by September 2027, 200 MW by January 2028, 310 MW by July 2028; rent is payable on the full 910 MW regardless of utilisation. Riot puts capital cost at about $6 million per IT MW ($5.5 billion), of which $4 million per MW is reimbursed to the tenant, funded by project debt or else as rent credits at 12% interest. With Rockdale (191 MW, same tenant) Anthropic is counterparty on 1,101 MW of Riot's 1,151 MW contracted. Caveat: the tenant installs and owns the modular compute; Texas sits under the extended state pause, though Corsicana's power is already developed. Country conversion: a gigawatt-class frontier-lab offtake in Texas after the election selloff. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Riot Platforms Q3 release and 10-Q, 4 Nov 2026; DCD, 9 Nov 2026; Bitcoin Magazine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Lambda names itself anchor of Alabama's Project Red Clay, a $33.1 billion, 1 GW campus in Lowndes County
item.description: Neocloud Lambda announced on 4 November 2026 that it will build the Red Clay Technology Center campus in Lowndes County, Alabama, near Montgomery, estimating $33.1 billion of investment in the state, more than 1,000 construction jobs and over 225 permanent roles. DCD reports the campus is planned at 1 GW, expandable to 1.5 GW, with power from Alabama Power pending regulatory approval, construction starting in Q1 2027 over up to five years, and first operations in Q4 2028; Cloverleaf documents commit to at least $16 billion of capital within seven years of service. Lambda says it will pay the full cost of power and grid infrastructure, use closed-loop cooling and fund a $10 million community benefits agreement. Caveat: power supply needs Alabama PSC approval and the $33.1 billion is Lambda's estimate. Country conversion: a gigawatt-class US neocloud campus lands in a state outside the newly flipped governor map. [Signal 56, Confirmed, via Lambda, 4 Nov 2026; DCD, 5 Nov 2026; WSFA; al.com] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Google commits an additional $15 billion to Malaysian data centres in 2027 and 2028
item.description: Alphabet president and chief investment officer Ruth Porat announced on 4 November 2026, with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, that Google will invest an additional $15 billion (RM61 billion) in Malaysia over 2027 and 2028. The money covers expansion of its Elmina Business Park campus in Selangor and new planned campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan. Google says it will work with Tenaga Nasional Berhad to add more than 1 GW of clean energy to the grid without public subsidies, and pay for its own power and grid connections; construction is projected to support 37,000 jobs a year. This builds on the $2 billion announced in May 2024 and the $160 million water plant announced 2 November. Caveat: no campus MW figures were disclosed by Google; DCD cites reports of 500 MW to 1 GW for Port Dickson. Country conversion: Malaysia lands a hyperscaler commitment more than seven times its 2024 pledge. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Malay Mail (Bernama), 4 Nov 2026; The Star; Straits Times; DCD] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Oracle reportedly scraps a $7 billion deal to lease up to 100,000 AI chips to Tencent in Southeast Asia
item.description: The Financial Times reported on 4 November 2026 that Oracle has cancelled a five-year contract worth about $7 billion under which Tencent would have leased access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips hosted in Oracle data centres in Southeast Asia, weeks after signing. Per the FT, US officials raised concerns with Oracle, while Guangdong officials asked Tencent to support domestic Chinese chips. The FT separately reported that Nvidia has verbally told data centre partners that at least 51% of their services must go to customers outside China. Caveat: single-source report based on anonymous sources; Oracle, Tencent and the White House had not commented. Country conversion: the offshore rental route for Chinese access to US accelerators is narrowing. [Signal 50, Single-source, via Financial Times, 4 Nov 2026, via DCD and The Business Times] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Portugal readies a decree requiring data centres to run on renewable power and avoid competing for fresh water
item.description: Environment and Energy Minister Maria da Graca Carvalho told a parliamentary hearing that the government is finalising rules, expected by year-end, under which data centres must secure renewable electricity and use either cooling that does not need fresh water or a water solution that does not conflict with public and economic supply, plus a very rigorous environmental review. Operators would not have to generate their own power but must guarantee renewable access and cover grid connection costs (SAPO). DCD counts more than 2.6 GW under development in Portugal, including the 1.2 GW Start Campus at Sines. Caveat: draft rules, final text not published. Country conversion: Portugal joins Spain in conditioning data centre growth on renewable supply. [Signal 40, Corroborated, via Reuters via Euronext, 4 Nov 2026; DCD; SAPO] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: South Korea plans a 2027 large-scale reference system pairing AMD CPUs and GPUs with Korean NPUs
item.description: At AMD's Advancing AI event in Seoul on 4 November 2026, Second Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Je-myung said the government will launch a 'K-AI Semiconductor Full-Stack Reference' support programme next year, linking domestic chips, models, software and services. Policy chief Lee Dogyu said the ministry will build a large-scale demonstration reference combining AMD CPUs and GPUs with homegrown NPUs for public institutions, companies and global customers. The ministry and AMD held an MOU steering committee the same day, covering an AMD AI research centre and talent programmes (Yonhap). Caveat: no budget, capacity or site was disclosed. Country conversion: Korea is building a non-Nvidia sovereign stack reference. [Signal 36, Corroborated, via Yonhap, 4 Nov 2026; Digital Daily; Asia Business Daily] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Goodman and Digital Realty offer A$715 million for 9.9% of NextDC after its Melbourne power delay
item.description: Goodman Group and Digital Realty offered A$715 million (about US$500 million) for a 9.9% stake in NextDC at A$9.50 a share, a 45.5% premium, via a term sheet lodged with the ASX after trading on 4 November 2026 (Reuters, DCD). NextDC shares had fallen as much as 45% in recent weeks after it deferred A$140 million of revenue because Jemena's network upgrade for its M3 Melbourne site, planned to take capacity from 60 MW to 225 MW, slipped to FY2027/28, and it paused new developments. The bidders say they will not seek control for now. Caveat: NextDC had not responded. Country conversion: Australia's largest listed operator is being recapitalised by rivals after a grid delay. [Signal 34, Corroborated, via DCD, 4 Nov 2026; Reuters] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Candidates pledging data centre pauses win governor races in Texas, Ohio and Georgia
item.description: In the 3 November 2026 US midterms, Democrat Gina Hinojosa ousted Texas governor Greg Abbott (AP), after campaigning for an immediate moratorium on new data centres until the legislature passes protections. In Ohio, Amy Acton, who backs a conditional moratorium requiring data centres to cover 100% of their utility costs, defeated Vivek Ramaswamy; in Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms, who called for a statewide pause on data centre development, won (AP). DCD reports 26 gubernatorial candidates in 21 of 36 states ran on anti-data centre platforms, and that Democrats took both chambers of Congress, with some results still being counted. Texas has about 6.5 GW under development per DCD. Caveat: the new governors take office in January 2027 and any moratorium needs legislation or executive action; Abbott's own temporary pause for the ERCOT large-load audit was already in place. Country conversion: the US build-out now faces executive-level opposition in three of its largest growth states. [Signal 66, Corroborated, via AP, 4 Nov 2026 (Texas, Georgia); DCD, 4 Nov 2026; Euronews] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Canada joins the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking as its 39th participating state
item.description: Canada joined the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking on 3 November 2026, giving Canadian researchers access to European HPC, AI and quantum computing resources provided by the JU, per DCD. AI Minister Evan Solomon said membership will open access to world-class supercomputing, AI and quantum resources. Other non-EU participants include the UK, Norway, Switzerland, Israel and Turkey. Caveat: no Canadian funding contribution or allocation size was disclosed. Country conversion: Canada adds shared European public compute access alongside its domestic sovereign compute programme. [Signal 28, Confirmed, via DCD, 3 Nov 2026; EuroHPC JU] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant plan GW-scale AI data centre at Drax Power Station; investment could exceed £20 billion
item.description: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant (Brookfield's UK AI infrastructure platform) announced on 3 November 2026 a partnership to develop, deliver and operate GW-scale data centre capacity at Drax Power Station in North Yorkshire, backed by the Brookfield-Qai AI infrastructure joint venture. Brookfield estimates total investment could exceed £20 billion, including about £2.5 billion for phase one. Phasing: up to 100 MW operational from Q1 2028, an ambition of 500 MW between 2028 and 2031, and more after 2031. The 1,000-acre estate has 4 GW of grid access and 2.6 GW of active dispatchable generation; the Guardian reports Drax hopes to power the site directly by the early 2030s. The partners say the plan aligns with the government's new Data Centre Covenant. Caveat: phase one is subject to planning, regulatory and network approvals and to securing a tenant; no tenant is named. Country conversion: an existing UK power station's grid connection is being repurposed for AI load. [Signal 60, Confirmed, via Drax Group press release, 3 Nov 2026; The Guardian, 3 Nov 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html
